Modern.brandNameRationale: The strop is the leather strip used to realign the edge of a straight razor between honings; lather is what the badger brush whips up from the shaving soap. Paired with an ampersand, the two trade objects ground the brand entirely in wet-shaving vocabulary.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern men's grooming has split between cartridge-razor mass brands and a small considered-wet-shaving cohort. The opening is for a brand that puts the strop and the lather bowl in the brand position and sells a small permanent kit.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Bevel (getbevel.com) holds the considered-modern Black grooming slot. Harry's (harrys.com) is the cartridge-DTC peer. Edwin Jagger (edwinjagger.com) plays the heritage wet-shaving peer. We sit closer to Edwin Jagger in posture with a sharper DTC framing.
Modern.positioningStatement: A modern wet-shaving brand organized around the strop, the brush, and the bowl.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 55. Has switched from a cartridge razor in the last five years. Reads Sharpologist. Owns a badger brush.

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark — Strop & Lather set in a clean modern grotesk, with a small drawn mark of a leather strop hanging over a lather bowl. The mark alone is the favicon.

typography.primary: Söhne for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: Söhne Mono for product specs and blade dimensions
typography.rationale: One family. Mono carries the technical razor data.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: The shaving mug holds the soap puck; the mirror is what the gentleman faced each morning. Paired with the definite article, they name the two objects of the inherited dressing-table shaving ritual. The brand is the ritual.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury men's grooming at the inherited-shaving-kit tier serves the buyer who wants the full ritual — strop, mug, brush, mirror, soap — in a single drawer. The product is a small permanent kit, finished by hand, signed by the maker.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: D.R. Harris (drharris.co.uk) is the institutional St. James's grooming benchmark. Acca Kappa (accakappa.com) holds the considered-Italian slot. Penhaligon's (penhaligons.com) plays the heritage-fragrance-and-shaving peer. We sit between D.R. Harris and Acca Kappa with a sharper ritual-object framing.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A heritage shaving house organized around the inherited dressing-table ritual.

typography.primary: Canela for the wordmark and the ritual guide

Minimal.brandNameRationale: A strop is the strip of leather used to realign the edge of a straight razor — single trade word, single syllable, terminal period. The brand is the object.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimal grooming brands have converged on pharmacy-white aesthetic. The opening underneath is a wet-shaving brand stripped to the tool itself — the strop — sold with the soap, the brush, and nothing else.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Frama Apothecary (framacph.com) holds the considered-Nordic apothecary peer slot. Aesop (aesop.com) sits in the considered-minimal grooming tier. Le Labo (lelabo.com) plays the considered-minimal scent peer. We sit closer to Frama with a sharper single-tool focus.
Minimal.positioningStatement: Wet shaving stripped to the strop, the soap, and the brush.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Bay rum is the heritage post-shave tonic — bay leaves, rum, and spice — that defined Caribbean and English barbershop grooming from the 19th century onward. Naming the firm after the foundational tonic and closing with Grooming Co. signals an old-firm contract grooming manufacturer.
Corporate.industrySummary: Contract grooming manufacturing is a serious B2B category. The buyers are barber-shop chains, hotel amenity programs, and private-label brand operators. The vendors compete on formula stability, fill capacity, and bottle sourcing.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Coty (coty.com) is the institutional grooming-manufacturer benchmark. Voyant Beauty (voyantbeauty.com) holds the contract-manufacturing slot. KIK Custom Products (kikcorp.com) plays the private-label peer. We sit smaller, sharper on the heritage-tonic formulary.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Contract grooming manufacturing organized around heritage formulas — bay rum, tallow soap, alum, witch hazel.

Creative.brandNameRationale: The badger-hair brush is the foundational wet-shave tool — the badger is the unlikely mascot. The Smiling Badger pairs the working tool with a friendly face, signaling a grooming brand with character rather than gravitas.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative grooming brands have crowded the apothecary-aesthetic space. The opening underneath is for a brand with an actual mascot — a smiling badger — and a small permanent kit sold with a sense of humor.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Dr. Squatch (drsquatch.com) holds the playful-DTC slot. Duke Cannon (dukecannon.com) sits in the heritage-humor peer position. Beardbrand (beardbrand.com) plays the considered-modern peer. We sit closer to Duke Cannon with a sharper mascot framing.
Creative.positioningStatement: A creative wet-shaving brand with the badger brush as the brand mascot.
